## Summary

I implemented the disposable-domain email blocklist by following the codebase's existing granular, one-concern-per-class validation pattern (mirroring `EmailNormalizer`/`InvalidEmailException`, `PostcodeValidator`/`InvalidPostcodeException`, etc.):

1. **`DisposableEmailDomainValidator`** — a small static utility with a single responsibility: reject an already-normalized email whose domain is on the blocklist (`mailinator.com`, `tempmail.com`, `guerrillamail.com`). It accepts `null` (email is optional). I kept this separate from `EmailNormalizer` because that class owns *syntactic* normalization, whereas this is a distinct *policy* check on a syntactically-valid address.

2. **`DisposableEmailDomainException`** — thrown by the validator, matching the existing exception convention.

3. **`ExceptionControllerAdvice.handleDisposableEmailDomainException`** — maps the exception to `400 Bad Request` with an `errors: ["email"]` body, identical in shape to the sibling email/telephone/postcode handlers.

4. **`OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`** — one added line invoking the validator right after `EmailNormalizer.normalize(...)`, so it runs on the canonical lower-cased address.

The new `AcceptanceTest.errorRejectsDisposableDomain` passes and the full suite is green.
